# Overview

The `lrmodel` package was designed to re-implement the base R function `lm()` 
and generate results from a linear regression model. This vignettes demonstrates 
how to use the package's core function, `lrmodel()`, to fit a linear regression
model and explore the results. It also includes a comparison of the correctness
and efficiency of `lrmodel()` vs. the base R function `lm()` using `all.equal()`
and `bench::mark()`.

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(lrmodel)
```

# Correctness

The correctness of the `lrmodel()` function is demonstrated below by comparing
the output of `lrmodel()` to the base R function `lm()` using `all.equal()`.

```{r}
all.equal(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients, 
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals
)

all.equal(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values
)
```

# Efficiency

The efficiency of `lrmodel()` vs. the base R function `lm()` is demonstrated 
below using `bench::mark()`.

```{r, out.width="75%"}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$coefficients
)
result
plot(result)
```

```{r, out.width="75%"}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$residuals
)
result
plot(result)
```

```{r, out.width="75%}
result <- bench::mark(
  lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values,
  lm(mpg ~ wt, mtcars)$fitted.values
)
result
plot(result)
```
